Q: Is there a way to have nodejs code coverage when tests are written in python (pytest)? A:

I hit the same issue, I have a full stack application which uses Python on the backend and JS in the frontend. Inspired by @hoefling's approach, I wrote
https://github.com/HDembinski/pytest-jscov
which let's you seamlessly write Playwright tests in Python and check their coverage, using Playwright's debugging features. The plugin works on Windows, MacOS, and Linux. Because it integrates seamlessly with pytest --cov, your AI agent can use it, and it also shows line coverage in VS Code.

Q: What is the significance of making a nested function global in Lua? A:

I looked at the Wikipedia article and your code, and I don't have a clue what that algorithm is doing, but I do know how defining Lua functions work.

Functions can be local or global variables; when you define function B inside function A, if you don't put local in front of the function definition, B is a global variable.

The other thing is upvalues. Every time Lua's control flow passes through a function definition, it creates a new "closure" of the function, with access to the local variables captured in that function (if there are any). (more info: https://www.lua.org/pil/6.1.html)

In your code, every time you call A, if B is defined as a global function, the global variable "B" is overwritten with the new closure. Then any further calls to B will call the latest definition of function B.

But when B is defined as a local function, it does not overwrite previous closures of B. Then any further calls to B depend on which closure of B is referenced.

Also note that if a variable is global, it never becomes an upvalue (since global variables only exist in the single _G table, while local variables can exist independently to each closure).

Q: Is there a way to hide output from the Taskkill command in a batch file for installing patches? A:

This is the solution that works for me in cmd console

taskkill /f /t /im test_program.exe 1>nul 2>&1

As a side note I found out that when using PowerShell (version 5.1) instead of cmd console nul phrase has to be replaced with $null phrase, otherwise there will be errors.

taskkill /f /t /im "test_program.exe" 1>$null 2>&1

/f stands for force - to end this process forcefully (killed by Windows)
/im stands for imagename - name of the process to end
/t probably stands for tree - to end also all child processes in this process subtree

It seems that in Windows there are standard streams which are numbered in the same way as in Linux.

0: stdin
1: stdout
2: stderr

2>&1 redirects standard error output of command to standard output of command
1>nul or 1>$null redirects standard output of command to "void", it becomes suppressed. This works similarly to redirecting to /dev/null in Linux.

Q: Query tuning: counting distinct matching rows across tables A:

Indeed, I was wondering if there is no alternative way to retrive the same results using a more efficient query without creating any indexes. do you have any ideas?

By analysing the execution plan (SQL server), the dominant cost arises from the 2 sort operations.

I have already tested another query (bellow) that avoids having 2 sorts (as shown in the execution plan), however, the reduction is not significant. The ESTC drops to 98, when the initial was around 101.

SELECT 
    pBoth.county, 
    COUNT(*) AS properties_sold_both_years
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT p24.county, p24.PAON, p24.street, p24.town
    FROM ShortPricePaidData2024 p24
    JOIN ShortPricePaidData2025 p25
        ON p25.county  = p24.county
        AND p25.PAON   = p24.PAON
        AND p25.street = p24.street
        AND p25.town   = p24.town
) pBoth
GROUP BY pBoth.county;
